title: Career roadmap · Policy Advisor
summary: Build from AI research and ethics into evidence-based technology policy, AI governance, regulatory analysis, responsible innovation and public-sector strategy.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes a 2026-start Ph.D. pathway. Early years build technical AI literacy, ethics and empirical policy research; later years focus on regulation, governance, strategic foresight and high-level advisory work.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Develop AI literacy, ethics, social-science research, policy analysis, technology assessment and quantitative evidence skills.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Own an AI-policy area such as AI governance, safety, privacy, algorithmic accountability, public-sector AI or digital rights.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead multidisciplinary policy programs connecting governments, regulators, industry, academia and civil society.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Advise on frontier AI governance while integrating technical evidence, law, economics, ethics, geopolitics and institutional strategy.

blocks.label: Typical planning ranges are

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

A senior Policy Advisor should be able to engage directly with technical AI researchers while advising decision-makers on regulatory and institutional consequences. Stay current with frontier AI, foundation models, autonomous systems, privacy-enhancing technologies, algorithmic auditing, AI safety and international AI governance. The goal is to turn uncertain technical developments into clear policy choices, implementation mechanisms and measurable safeguards.
